data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: unknown

observations.finding: treated fields f_52a5ba54a4cf and f_daa3056c4390 show markedly lower confluence and larger cell-free areas vs same-plate DMSO f_bd4169e2e78f. Cells are isolated/spread, not epithelial sheet. Estimated ~1/3 density by eye.

DNA stain (blue) visible in composite only - no separate DAPI gray channel provided. Nuclei appear sparse, isolated, some modestly larger vs crowded round nuclei in DMSO. No obvious multinucleation, fragmentation or prominent mitotic enrichment visible in composite.

beta-tubulin read as green in composite, no separate grayscale provided, with yellow overlap where actin co-localizes. Treated cells show brighter, more heterogeneous green cytoplasm with sharper cell-to-background texture vs dimmer diffuse green in confluent DMSO. Spiky/elongated cell shapes present, e.g. long thin extension lower-center f_52a5ba54a4cf.

F-actin read as red in composite, no separate grayscale provided. Treated cells retain distinct peripheral red signal often with spiky protrusions/lamellipodia at edges; contrast between red cell rim and black background markedly higher than DMSO where red is faint intercellular mesh in dense monolayer.

Cell shape: DMSO = polygonal tightly packed epithelial morphology. Treated = mixed rounded, spindle and stellate with prominent extensions and isolated placement. No clear bundles, asters, or loss of filament network diagnostic in composite resolution.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Pattern is low cell count + modest nuclear enlargement + high variance/contrast in both tubulin and actin on composites. DMSO is confluent; sparsity alone increases std/contrast vs background. No selective actin loss (Actin disruptors), no microtubule bundling/ depolymerization with mitotic arrest (Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers), no clear enlarged/multinucleate (Aurora) phenotype. General cytotoxic / stress morphology only.

report.uncertainty: Only 1024x819px composites available this time, no separate grayscale DAPI/tubulin/actin channels. Green/red discrimination and nuclear size by eye limited by overlap (yellow) and confluence difference. Strong quantitative deviations: cell_count z=-6.57 value 104.5 vs DMSO median 316.5; nuc_area z=6.82 895 vs 809; frac_large_nucleus z=6.92 0.028 vs 0.008; tub_mean z=13.77 0.424 vs 0.284, tub_std z=15.95 0.225 vs 0.117, tub_glcm_contrast z=28.87 0.004 vs 0.002; act_std z=15.01 0.14 vs 0.075, act_glcm_contrast z=22.63 0.002 vs 0.001. All |z|>6 = strong vs plate DMSO and directionally consistent with visual lower density/brighter more textured staining, but texture metrics are non-specific and inflated by sparsity. Do not support any single listed MoA; compound identity not guessable.

data.note:
Reflection note:
- Unblinded compound AZ258 (PubChem CID 59396138, N-(2,3-difluorophenyl)-2-[4-[[7-methoxy-5-[[(2R)-pyrrolidin-2-yl]methoxy]quinazolin-4-yl]amino]pyrazol-1-yl]acetamide) has no curated ChEMBL mechanism; BBBC021 annotates as Aurora kinase inhibitors.
- My blinded conclusion Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.88) was scored correct by code.
- Evidence: extreme polyploidy phenotype at 0.3 µM (frac_large_nucleus z=80.7, nuc_area z=42.6) and 1 µM (frac_large_nucleus z=70.3, nuc_area z=38.0) with irregular nuclei, doubled DNA content and increased cell area (e3,e8); microscopist confirmed enlarged irregular nuclei / cytokinesis failure pattern (e6) without microtubule bundle loss; atlas NSC 2/4 and k-neighbors 9/10 Aurora (e9, mean similarity 0.881, per-well 0.971 at 0.3 µM).
- High dose 30 µM shift to toxicity/low count but still Aurora-like profile; intermediate 10 µM maintained large nuclei/DNA content consistent with dose-response.
- Literature search for Aurora inhibitor polyploidy returned PMID 30050055 (AURORA-A loss associated with multinucleation) and secondary hit PMID 22555221, supporting polyploidy as Aurora phenotype, though assay-specific chemical probe literature for AZ258 is not indexed in PubChem/ChEMBL.

reflection.text: Reflection after unblinding AZ258 (CID 59396138, no curated mechanism) as Aurora kinase inhibitors - verdict correct (p=0.88, approved): What the evidence got right: The nuclear size/polyploidy signal was diagnostic and dose-coherent. Wells w_7d742a2ea2 (1 uM, e3: frac_large_nucleus z=+70.3, nuc_area +38.0, nuc_major_axis +22.7, 350 cells) and w_8b561f0561 (0.3 uM, e8: frac_large_nucleus +80.7, nuc_area +42.6, major_axis +27.6, 421 cells) showed extreme enlargement consistent with Aurora inhibition-associated multinucleation/polyploidy described in literature PMID 30050055, while w_b09894f4c4 (10 uM, e7: nuc_area +25.2) and w_bb49de52e8 (30 uM, e2: 165 cells) showed declining nuclear phenotype and cell count, indicating bell-shaped response with toxicity at top dose. The microscopist review on mid-dose (e6: 4 fields, 12 observations, density lower, candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors, DNA replication) independently flagged the same candidates, and compare_to_reference_atlas converged twice: e4 (2 wells: NSC 1/2 Aurora, kNN 9/10 Aurora) and e9 (4 wells: NSC 2/4 Aurora, kNN 9/10 Aurora, 1/10 DNA damage/Protein degradation). Those kNN 9/10 votes were the strongest quantitative anchor. Acquisition strategy was efficient given 4 wells left over 8 doses (e1): sampling high (30 uM) for maximal effect then mid (1 uM) captured the unexpected divergence between tubulin texture and nuclear enlargement, and bridging 10 uM and 0.3 uM mapped the peak at 0.3-1 uM without wasting wells on subactive 0.01-0.1 uM doses. What misled or could have misled: e2 at 30 uM (tub_glcm_contrast +28.9, act_glcm_contrast +22.6, tub_std +15.9) mimics microtubule perturbagen texture and was correctly listed as contradicting evidence for Aurora in hypothesis_history step 13. We retained Microtubule stabilizers 0.03 and DNA replication/DNA damage at low probability but did not overweight this, because e3/e6/e8 dominated. The dose_response summaries e10 (nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0) and e11 (frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2) are negative monotonic over the 0.3-30 uM window we sampled; this is not inverse dose-dependence but the descending limb of a bell curve after the polyploidy peak, and cell number loss (421 -> 350 -> 203 -> 165) supports cytotoxicity confounding at high dose. What we missed / did not prove: e12 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6 was non-significant over 4 wells, so we did not demonstrate the 4N/8N DNA content doubling expected for Aurora vs DNA replication polyploidy. We flagged this in the proposed next experiment (pHH3 Ser10 + DNA content flow vs reference Aurora and Microtubule stabilizer controls) but had no direct biochemical confirmation in-run. Literature search e17/e18 returned only 2 hits and we did not have independent imaging validation beyond the two describe_phenotype calls (e5 2 fields/5 obs 'unknown' was uninformative). Overall, the decision to prioritize massive frac_large_nucleus + nuc_area + atlas kNN convergence over isolated high-dose tubulin contrast was correct and would replicate.

We retained Microtubule stabilizers 0.03 and DNA replication/DNA damage at low probability but did not overweight this, because e3/e6/e8 dominated. The dose_response summaries e10 (nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0) and e11 (frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2) are negative monotonic over the 0.3-30 uM window we sampled; this is not inverse dose-dependence but the descending limb of a bell curve after the polyploidy peak, and cell number loss (421 -> 350 -> 203 -> 165) supports cytotoxicity confounding at high dose. What we missed / did not prove: e12 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.40 p=0.6 was non-significant over 4 wells, so we did not demonstrate the 4N/8N DNA content doubling expected for Aurora vs DNA replication polyploidy. We flagged this in the proposed next experiment (pHH3 Ser10 + DNA content flow vs reference Aurora and Microtubule stabilizer controls) but had no direct biochemical confirmation in-run. Literature search e17/e18 returned only 2 hits and we did not have independent imaging validation beyond the two describe_phenotype calls (e5 2 fields/5 obs 'unknown' was uninformative).
